lines.text: תַּחַשׁ, וַתַּחַשׁ for וַתָּחָשׁ, 3 pers. fut. Kal
from r. חוּשׁ; for an analogous instance
see under r. עִיט p. 770. Job 31, 5.
תֵּחַת Prov. 17, 10, fut. Kal of r. נָחַת q. v.
תֵּט fut. apoc. Kal from r. נָטָה, for תִּטֶּה.
תֵּיעָשֶׂה Ex. 25, 31 in many editions, with
Yod as ‘mater lectionis,’ for תֵּעָשֶׂה;
but contrary to rule and almost cer-
tainly a corruption. Lgb. 52, 331.
תֵּכַהּ, וַתֵּכַהּ, fut. apoc. Kal for תִּכְהֶה,
from r. כָּהָה.
תְּכַס fut. apoc. Pi. for תְּכַסֶּה, from r. כָּסָה.
תֵּלַהּ, וַתֵּלַהּ, fut. apoc. Kal from r. לָהַהּ.
תָּלַן fut. Kal shortened from תָּלִין, from
r. לוּן or לִין.
תֶּמְחִי for תַּמְחֶה 2 masc. (the Yod be-
longs to the root) of fut. Hiph. from
מָחָה to wipe away. Jer. 18, 23.
תַּמְנוּ Chald. 1 pl. præt. r. תָּמַם, for תַּמּוֹנוּ,
Num. 17, 28. Lehrg. 373.—Also for
3 pl. תַּמּוּ Lam. 3, 22; so Ewald and
Roediger.
תֶּמֶס, וַתֶּמֶס, fut. apoc. Hiph. from r. מָסָה
to flow down.
תַּמֵּר Ex. 23, 21, fut. Hiph. see מָרַר Hiph.
note, p. 620.
תֹּמְרוּ for תֹּאמְרוּ fut. Kal from r. אָמַר.
תֵּן, תְּנָה, imp. Kal from r. נָתַן q. v.
תִּנְדַּע, see יִנְדַּע.
תֹּנוּ fut. Hiph. of r. יָנָה q. v.
תֹּסֵף for תֹּאסֵף fut. Kal from r. אָסַף.
תֵּעָגֵנָה for תֵּעָגֵנָּה 2 plur. fut. Niph. from
r. עָגַן, Dag. forte being omitted; see
above in חָיָה. § 66. note 11.
תְּעֻגֶּנָה Ez. 4. 12, fut. Kal c. suff. from r.
עוּג q. v. Dag. forte euphon. in ג.
תֹּפֵהוּ, וַתֹּפֵהוּ, fut. Kal from r. אָפָה to
bake, for תֹּאפֵהוּ.
תְּפוֹצוֹתִיכֶם Jer. 25, 34, see under the root
פּוּץ, note.
תִּצַּלְנָה Jer. 19, 3, fut. Kal from r. צָלַל,
for the comm. תִּצְלֶינָה. See צָלַל I.
תראנה 1 Sam. 14, 27 Keth. (by a cor-
ruption) for תָּאֹרְנָה. The copyist
seems to have had in mind the word
תִּרְאֶינָה.
תֵּרֶב, וַתֵּרֶב, fut. apoc. Kal from r. רָבָה.
תֵּרוֹץ fut. Niph. from r. רָצַץ to break,
the form being borrowed from רוּץ.
תִּרְצֹנָה Prov. 23, 26, i. e. for Keri תִּצֹּרְנָה
fut. Kal of r. נָצַר. The Keth. is
fut. Kal of r. רוּץ, and should be read
תָּרֹצְנָה.
תִּשֶּׂנָה Jer. 9, 17 for תִּשֶּׂאנָה fut. Kal from
r. נָשָׂא.
תֶּשִׁי Deut. 32, 18, see r. שָׁיָה p. 1055.
תֵּשְׁתְּ fut. apoc. Kal from r. שָׁתָה to
drink.
תִּשְׁתַּחוּ fut. apoc. sing. Hithp. for תִּשְׁתַּחֲוֶה,
from r. שָׁחָה to bow down.
תִּשְׁתָּע Is. 41, 10, fut. apoc. Hithp. from
r. שָׁעָה.
תֵּת inf. Kal from r. נָתַן to give, contract-
ed for תֶּנֶת. With suff. תִּתִּי.
תִּתָּבָר 2 Sam. 22, 27, for תִּתְבָּרַר fut.
Hithp. from r. בָּרַר. Lgb. p. 374.
תַּתָּה by aphæresis for נָתַתָּה, which is
read Ps. 18, 41. Comp. רַד for יָרַד.
תַּתִּי, see in תַּת above.
תִּתַּם, תִּתֹּם, fut. Kal from תָּמַם, q. v.
תתן 1 K. 17, 14 Keth. commonly taken
for תֵּת to give, with Nun parag. as
in 1 K. 6, 19, where however תִּתֵּן is
future. Here the Keri, הַתְּ, is to be
preferred.
תֵּתַע, וַתֵּתַע, fut. apoc. Kal from r. תָּעָה.
תִּתַּפָּל 2 Sam. 22, 27, see in פָּתַל Hithp.
תֵּתַצַּב Ex. 2, 4, for תִּתְיַצֵּב Hithp. from
r. יָצַב. Lgb. 386.

line_status.note: First word has patach (flat stroke) under the dageshed tav, not qamets; in the third word the chet carries a qamets (vertical tail visible), matching the regular ayin-vav form וַתָּחָשׁ with retracted tone that the shortened וַתַּחַשׁ stands for.
Under the initial tav two horizontal dots (tsere) are printed, not a single patach; so תֵּחַת (Reading B), matching Prov. 17:10 fut. Kal of נָחַת.
Under the initial tav the print shows two dots side by side (tsere), not a horizontal patah stroke; the rest of the line is identical in both readings and matches the print.

The print shows tsere (two dots) under the dageshed tav and patach under the kaf in both apocopated forms (תֵּכַהּ / וַתֵּכַהּ), not hiriq under tav and tsere under kaf as in Reading A; the final תִּכְהֶה is the same in both.
The final root word is printed with a mappiq (dot) in the last he and patah under the middle he — לָהַהּ, matching Reading B; Reading A's לָהָה (qamets, no mappiq) is not what is printed.

Under the lamed of the first word the print shows a single short horizontal bar (patach), not two separate dots (tsere); compare the clearly dotted tsere/segol forms on the line above. Reading A (תָּלַן) is correct; everything else in both readings matches the print.
Under the tav of the second word the print shows a horizontal stroke (patach), not a hiriq dot; fits "fut. Hiph." תַּמְחֶה. Rest of line identical in both readings.
The last word is printed with a plene vav (ḥolem-vav) after a single dageshed mem — תַּמּוֹנוּ, five letters — not the six-letter תָּמַמְנוּ with two mems that Reading A gives.

Both dalets show a dot inside the letter (dagesh lene after quiescent shewa in נְדּ), so Reading A's דַּ is correct; B omits the dagesh. All else (hiriq under tav with dagesh, shewa under nun, patah, qamets-less final ayin, punctuation) is identical in both and matches the print.
Middle letter is gimel (ג) with its projecting foot, not nun; the root עגן fits the entry (תֵּעָגֵנָה Ruth 1:13, with dagesh forte omitted).
The gimel carries a printed dagesh (a dot is visible inside the ג), which the following line confirms: "Dag. forte euphon. in ג". Reading A omits it.

The tav carries a dot above it (holem) with dagesh inside, and the aleph is quiescent with no hataf segol beneath; the only sub-linear points are the tsere under pe. Reading B's segol + hataf segol are not printed.
First word has tsere (two dots) under the tav, same as in וַתֵּרֶב; Reading A's segol is wrong.

Decisive difference is the first word's pointing: the print shows shewa under resh and holem over tsade (תִּרְצֹנָה), not holem over resh with shewa under tsade as in Reading A. The Keri form תִּצֹּרְנָה is identical in both readings and matches the print.
The nun carries a qamets (T-shaped mark), not a hireq, and the following tav has patach with no dagesh; the print reads נָתַתָּה (Qal "thou hast given"), as in Reading A.
Under the first tav of both תַּתִּי and תַּת the print shows a single horizontal stroke (patach), not the dot of hiriq or the two dots of tsere; Reading B matches, Reading A does not.

The first (rightmost) Hebrew item has hiriq under the first tav and dagesh + patach under the second (תִּתַּם); the second item has hiriq under the first tav and a holem dot above the second tav (תִּתֹּם). Reading A reverses the order and gives a qamets that is not printed.
Right-hand letter is ה (detached left leg, no foot) with patach; left-hand letter is תּ with dagesh and shewa. No tsere and no second ת, so Reading A's תֵּת is wrong; Reading B matches the print.
